title: ELISA-Based Enzyme Kinetics Assay for Measuring cGAS Activity
author: Cécile Fréreux
license_note: PMC full-text XML — Bio-protocol — CC-BY confirmed in article XML

steps.title: Prepare 4× Reaction Buffer
steps.instruction: Combine 200 µL Tris‑HCl pH 7.5 (1 M, Fisher BioReagents, cat BP152‑5), 50 µL MgCl₂ (1 M, Sigma‑Aldrich, cat 208337), 10 µL Tween‑20 (10 %, Fisher BioReagents, cat BP337‑500) and 4.74 mL nuclease‑free water (Thermo Scientific, cat J71786.XCR) in a tube to a final volume of 5 mL (final concentrations: 40 mM Tris‑HCl, 10 mM MgCl₂, 0.02 % Tween‑20). Prepare fresh before use or store at 4 °C ≤3 months, or aliquot and store at –20 °C ≤6 months.

steps.title: Dilute His‑cGAS 1:10
steps.instruction: In a 0.2 mL PCR tube mix 20 µL His‑cGAS (10 µM, Cayman Chemical, cat 22810), 50 µL 4× reaction buffer (from step 1) and 130 µL nuclease‑free water to a total of 200 µL (final 1 µM His‑cGAS). Perform immediately before the kinetic experiment; aliquot ~5 µL and store at –80 °C ≤1 month. Use each aliquot once and avoid freeze‑thaw cycles.

steps.title: Anneal cGAS DNA Ligand
steps.instruction: Mix forward and reverse oligonucleotides each at 100 µM (ordered from Eurofins) in a 1:1 molar ratio. Heat the mixture in a beaker of boiling water with stirring to fully denature, then allow it to cool gradually to room temperature for at least 5 h or overnight. The resulting double‑stranded DNA has a final concentration of 50 µM and can be diluted with nuclease‑free water for use in the reactions (step 8).

steps.title: Equilibrate Reagents to RT
steps.instruction: Bring all reagents (water, 4× buffer, ATP, GTP, DNA ligand, test molecule) to room temperature. Keep recombinant proteins (His‑cGAS and any cofactors) on ice until just before use.

steps.title: Pre‑heat Incubator to 37 °C
steps.instruction: Set a thermocycler or tube incubator to 37 °C and allow it to reach the set temperature before adding reactions.

steps.title: Set Up EDTA Quench Tubes
steps.instruction: Dispense 8 µL of 55 mM EDTA (Sigma‑Aldrich, cat ED‑100G) into each 0.2 mL PCR tube (one tube per enzymatic reaction). Five microliters of each EDTA tube will be used later to stop the reactions (step 11).

steps.title: Assemble Reaction Master Mix
steps.instruction: For each pair of reactions (control + test) prepare a master mix in a PCR tube: 19.8 µL nuclease‑free water, 27.5 µL 4× reaction buffer (from step 1, giving 2× final concentration), 2.2 µL ATP 5 mM (Cayman, cat 40182, final 200 µM), 2.2 µL GTP 5 mM (Cayman, cat 16060, final 200 µM), and 3.3 µL His‑cGAS 1 µM (from step 2, final 60 nM). Total volume = 55 µL. Thaw a single 5 µL aliquot of His‑cGAS immediately before use; do not refreeze and discard any remaining enzyme.

steps.title: Dispense Mix and Add Test Molecule/DNA
steps.instruction: Label two PCR tubes “control” and “test”. Add 25 µL of the master mix (step 7) to each tube. To the test tube add the test molecule (e.g., 3 µL of a 1 µM protein → 60 nM final concentration) and adjust with nuclease‑free water so that each tube contains 48.5 µL before DNA addition. Keep the DNA ligand stock at 0.5 mM; add 1.5 µL to each tube last (gives 15 nM final for this example; vary as required). The final reaction (50 µL) contains 10 mM Tris‑HCl pH 7.5, 2.5 mM MgCl₂, 0.005 % Tween‑20, 30 nM His‑cGAS, 100 µM ATP, 100 µM GTP, variable DNA ligand and test molecule.

steps.title: Initiate Reaction by Adding DNA
steps.instruction: Using a multichannel pipette, add the DNA ligand to both control and test tubes simultaneously (step 8). This addition marks time zero (t = 0).

steps.title: Incubate Reaction at 37 °C
steps.instruction: Immediately place the tubes in the pre‑heated 37 °C thermocycler or incubator. Incubate for the desired duration (typical linear range: 30 s to 2 min; e.g., 30 s, 1 min, 1.5 min, 2 min). Reactions may also be performed at room temperature, but enzymatic activity may be reduced.

steps.title: Quench Reaction with EDTA
steps.instruction: After incubation, add 5 µL of 55 mM EDTA (from step 6) to each 50 µL reaction using a multichannel pipette. Mix by flicking and briefly centrifuge. The final volume is 55 µL and the final EDTA concentration is 5 mM. Samples can be stored at –20 °C short‑term or processed immediately.

steps.title: Verify Linear Product Formation
steps.instruction: Repeat steps 1‑10 at multiple time points (30 s, 1 min, 1.5 min, 2 min) using low (10 nM) and high (500 nM) DNA ligand concentrations to confirm that 2′3′‑cGAMP accumulation is linear with time under your specific conditions.

steps.title: Perform Michaelis‑Menten DNA Titration
steps.instruction: After linearity is confirmed, choose a fixed incubation time (e.g., 30 s) and run reactions across a range of DNA ligand concentrations (2.5, 5, 7.5, 15, 50, 500 nM) for both control and test conditions. Perform each reaction in at least duplicate, preferably triplicate, to generate reliable Michaelis‑Menten curves for Vmax, kcat and K½.

steps.title: Conduct 2′3′‑cGAMP ELISA
steps.instruction: Follow the manufacturer’s protocol for the 2′3′‑cGAMP ELISA kit (Cayman Chemical, cat 501700). Load 50 µL of each quenched reaction (from step 11) into ELISA wells. Incubate 2 h at room temperature (or overnight at 4 °C). No dilution of samples is required under the conditions described.
